item1_3_reconstructedOrphanConfigs.whatCouldNotBeRecoveredAcrossAllThree: whether a fresh `docker build` using the recovered args reproduces the currently-live image digest byte-for-byte. Two concrete, named reasons it might not: (1) Dockerfile's `FROM node:20-slim` is a mutable tag, not digest-pinned; (2) Dockerfile runs `npm install --omit=dev`, not `npm ci` -- package-lock.json exists but npm install does not strictly bind to it the way npm ci does. These three files are therefore high-confidence REBUILD PATHS, not proven bit-identical reproductions. Only running `gcloud builds submit` would settle it, and this lane does not run that.

LESSON: Dockerfile ARG->ENV values (build-time provenance like ENGINE_SHA/LDT_SHA) are invisible to `gcloud run jobs describe` -- that only returns runtime env vars set via --set-env-vars/--set-secrets. They ARE recoverable, read-only, no image pull, via `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>@<digest> --format '{{json .Image.Config}}'` (requires `gcloud auth configure-docker <registry>` first). This is the difference between 'unrecoverable, must guess' and 'recoverable, verify against upstream commits' for a reconstruction task -- worth trying before writing a config with placeholder or copied-from-a-similar-job build args.

gcloud run jobs execute --args overrides the deploy-time default for a single execution (confirmed via --help text, not assumed): 'If provided, an execution will be created with the input values. Otherwise, the existing arguments of the job are used.' No --update-secrets flag exists at execute time -- only --args and --update-env-vars. This means a writer whose secret/env needs already match an EXISTING job's bindings is executable today via that job, with no new deploy, regardless of whether any cloudbuild file's own default --args names its subcommand. An instrument (or a planner) checking only DEPLOY-time --args for 'deployability' will over-report undeployable writers whose real gap is documentation, not infrastructure.

A repo's own shell-variable indirection patterns are not uniform: cloudbuild.publish.yaml varies the JOB NAME itself in a for-loop (`deploy "$$JOB"`), not just the --args value (which the pre-existing sibling instrument already resolved). A new instrument parsing the same class of file needs its own resolution pass and its own violation test proving that resolution -- copying the sibling instrument's args-only resolution logic silently would have shipped 5 false positives.

A writer's own module docstring 'Triggers:' line is a claim, not a fact -- two of six writers here (parcel-value-history, vh-collision-remediate) name a trigger job that does not exist live and has no execution history. Cross-check every such claim against `gcloud run jobs list` before propagating it into a disposition.
